q: Why does (x − 2)(x + 3) = 0 give x = 2 or x = −3?
o: A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero
Because you set each bracket equal to the other

why: This zero-product rule is the reason we factorise at all.
The zero rule only works when the right side is 0. Expand: x² + x − 6 = 6, so x² + x − 12 = 0 = (x + 4)(x − 3), giving x = −4 or x = 3.
